title: Monetary Policy Report—January 2026
summary: The Bank of Canada's January 2026 Monetary Policy Report indicates the Canadian economy is continuing to adjust to US tariffs and the new global trade landscape, with growth expected to remain modest over the projection period. The Report projects inflation will remain near the 2% target. The adjustment process is characterized as one that will take time.
key_points: Canadian economy continues to adjust to US tariffs and new global trade landscape
Growth is expected to be modest during the projection period
Inflation is projected to remain near the 2% target
The adjustment to tariffs is expected to take time
why_it_matters: This report signals that the Bank of Canada expects continued economic headwinds from US trade policy while maintaining its inflation mandate. The near-target inflation projection suggests the BoC sees limited need for urgent policy action to address price pressures, potentially leaving room for accommodation if growth weakens further.
macro_context: The report centers on trade-related economic adjustment. US tariffs represent a significant macro catalyst affecting Canada's export-oriented economy. The near-target inflation outlook gives the Bank flexibility to support growth if needed, but the modest growth projection suggests the BoC is not anticipating a strong economic rebound in the near term.
